title_en: Great Poems and Songs (16/20): Meng Haoran and "Spring Dawn"
note_en: 了 at the end of a sentence can mark a new situation rather than a finished action: 天已经亮了 "it's already light" (it was dark before, and now it isn't). Here 亮 "bright" is an adjective, and since Chinese adjectives work as predicates without "to be," 了 alone signals the change, much like English "has gotten" or "now."

sentences.en: The poem has four lines: "Sleeping in spring, I miss the dawn; everywhere I hear the birds. Last night came the sound of wind and rain—who knows how many flowers fell?"
